paragraphs.source_en: Sansa felt as though she were in a dream. “Joffrey is dead,” she told the trees, to see if that would wake her.

paragraphs.source_en: He had not been dead when she left the throne room. He had been on his knees, though, clawing at his throat, tearing at his own skin as he fought to breathe. The sight of it had been too terrible to watch, and she had turned and fled, sobbing. Lady Tanda had been fleeing as well. “You have a good heart, my lady,” she said to Sansa. “Not every maid would weep so for a man who set her aside and wed her to a dwarf.”
